aerowarptics.guide.page.modulator_look.w: Everything changes with it: the aperture, the corridor wash, the exit shockwave.

aerowarptics.guide.page.wiring.split: Choose at the table. Launch with redstone. Diagnose at the drive.
aerowarptics.guide.page.wiring.title: Three Jobs, Three Places
aerowarptics.jei.info.astrolabe: Laid flat in a square, these form a Cartography Table. One block on its own is already a working table; two by two and three by three chart proportionally more ground, and a smaller table is absorbed when you build a bigger one around it. Right-click the finished table for a chart of every anchor within reach, drawn over a survey of the ground around it. It can ride aboard the ship.
aerowarptics.jei.info.handbook: Every machine in this mod, in the order you would build them. Right-click to open it; the ribbons along the top are the chapters.
aerowarptics.jei.info.rift_beacon: Bind a Rift Beacon by sneaking and right-clicking the Rift Drive of a ship you are standing on. After that, aim at anywhere within sight and right-click, and that ship warps to it - you do not have to be aboard, or anywhere near it. Binding is the moment permission is checked, so a bound beacon is a key: whoever holds it can call the ship. The summon itself still needs everything an ordinary warp needs - rotation, charge, range, and somewhere the hull actually fits.
aerowarptics.jei.info.rift_chute: Pairs with another Rift Chute anywhere in the world, including one bolted to an airship. Items travel both ways along the pair. Fit a Create funnel to any face to fill it - a chute is an inventory, not a belt attachment. Whichever end sends pays the Rift Essence, charged per item, so a drop-off needs no supply of its own. A full far end, an unloaded chunk or a ship mid-warp all make items wait in the chute rather than being lost.
aerowarptics.jei.info.rift_core: The machinery every Rift Drive is built around.
aerowarptics.jei.info.rift_drive: Built into an airship, a Rift Drive folds the whole hull to a Warp Anchor. Rotational force charges it; a jump spends a share of that charge, and costs more for distance and for weight. A drive standing on the ground has nothing to move.
aerowarptics.jei.info.rift_essence: What a rift sheds when a hull is folded through it. Caught by a Spatial Siphon aboard the ship, and spent dialling Rift Gates.
aerowarptics.jei.info.rift_gate: The one block of a Rift Gate that thinks. It counts as frame, so it may sit anywhere in the ring. Rift Essence pays to dial and keeps the doorway standing afterwards, and rotational force holds it - both only at the end that dialled. Run the tank dry, or let the shaft stall, and the gate hangs up. There has to be a second gate, in the same world, to reach.
aerowarptics.jei.info.rift_gate_frame: Builds the ring of a Rift Gate: standing upright, closed, and enclosing an empty opening of between four and two hundred and twenty-five blocks. That opening is the size limit for anything travelling through.
aerowarptics.jei.info.rift_goggles: Create's goggles with a rift-ground lens in them. They read machines exactly as the engineer's pair does, and they show Rift Fissures - tears in the world that are invisible to anyone not wearing them.
aerowarptics.jei.info.rift_lens: Focuses a rift. Used by everything here that has to aim one.
aerowarptics.jei.info.rift_modulator: Bolted beside a Rift Drive, a Rift Modulator lets its pilot choose the colour and the theme of the rift the drive tears - the aperture, the corridor wash, the exit shockwave, and even how it tears open in the first place, all of it. Right-click for a swatch of sixteen colours (left click for the core, right click for the rim) and a button that cycles twelve themes, seven of which are shameless nods to jumps you have seen elsewhere; shift-click the button to cycle backwards. Those seven bring their own colours rather than the swatch's - hyperspace is blue and white whatever you pick. It spends a trickle of Rift Essence while the linked drive is actually running a warp, and only then; run the tank dry, or take the drive away, and the rift falls straight back to the drive's own tier colours. A Display Link pointed at the Modulator reads the drive it is dressing, the same eight readouts the drive itself offers.
aerowarptics.jei.info.rift_probe: Scans a direction and distance for ground nobody has stood on, and brings back the same map the Astrolabe draws of an anchor. It is the only way to reach somewhere unexplored. Rift Essence pays for each scan; a Rift Drive on the same ship flies the course it finds.
aerowarptics.jei.info.singularity_core: A core collapsed in on itself. Only the Singularity drive is built on one.
aerowarptics.jei.info.spatial_siphon: Carried aboard an airship, a siphon catches the Rift Essence a completed warp sheds. Longer jumps are worth more, and every siphon aboard rolls for its own share. Holds four buckets, and pipes can draw it off.
aerowarptics.jei.info.stabiliser_ring: Holds a warp corridor open while a hull is still inside it.
aerowarptics.jei.info.warp_anchor: Marks a place an airship can be sent. Right-click to name it and to say who may travel there. The world keeps the record rather than the block, so an anchor stays a valid destination while its chunks are unloaded. Leave room for the arriving hull.
aerowarptics.message.anchor_limit_reache: You have reached this server's Warp Anchor limit
aerowarptics.message.anchor_name_taken: That anchor name is already in use
aerowarptics.message.anchor_not_yours: You do not own this anchor
aerowarptics.ponder.astrolabe.text_1: Astrolabe blocks are laid flat, in a square up to three by three
aerowarptics.ponder.astrolabe.text_2: Complete the square and the table forms itself
aerowarptics.ponder.astrolabe.text_3: Right-click for the chart: every anchor within reach, drawn over a survey of the ground around it
aerowarptics.ponder.astrolabe.text_4: A table can ride aboard the ship, so a course can be set without landing first
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_beacon.text_1: A Rift Beacon calls a ship you are not standing on, which is the one thing a course cannot do
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_beacon.text_2: Sneak and right-click a Rift Drive to bind the beacon to it. A plain click would only open the console
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_beacon.text_3: This is where you are checked. A beacon cannot be bound to a ship you could not have commanded by hand
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_beacon.text_4: Then aim anywhere in reach of the eye and right-click. The ship is called to whatever the crosshair is on
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_beacon.text_5: The drive still has to agree: turning fast enough, charged, in range, and with room for the hull to arrive
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_beacon.text_6: Refused, it says which of those failed, in the same words the drive's own console uses
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_beacon.text_7: Take the drive apart and the beacon is pointing at nothing. Bind it again to whatever you build next
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_chute.text_1: A Rift Chute hands items to another chute, however far apart they are - including one bolted to an airship
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_chute.text_2: Fit a funnel to any face and feed it from a belt. A chute is an inventory - it does not sit on the belt itself
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_chute.text_3: Right-click a chute to name it and pair it with another. Items travel both ways along a pair
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_chute.text_4: Whichever end sends pays the Rift Essence, per item and only when one crosses. A drop-off needs no supply of its own
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_chute.text_5: Nothing is ever lost. A full far end, an unloaded chunk or a ship mid-warp all make items wait in the chute instead
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_drive.text_1: A Rift Drive moves an entire airship to a Warp Anchor, hull and cargo and crew together
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_drive.text_2: It has to be built into the ship. A drive standing on the ground has nothing to move
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_drive.text_3: Rotational force spins it up. Below the drive's minimum speed it will not charge at all
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_drive.text_4: Charge builds while it turns. A jump spends a share of it - more for distance, more for a heavy ship
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_drive.text_5: Right-click for the console: pick an anchor, and the drive quotes the cost before committing
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_drive.text_6: Mk I to Singularity buy reach, speed and efficiency. The Singularity pays for its range with an unsteady arrival
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_fissure.text_1: Ruins generate where somebody's gate went wrong: a broken ring, a sunken vault, a survey mast
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_fissure.text_2: A Rift Fissure hangs in the middle of one. It is a tear that never closed, still leaking Rift Essence
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_fissure.text_3: It is invisible. No model, no outline, nothing to walk into - you can stand in the ruin and never know
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_fissure.text_4: Wear Rift Infused Goggles. Only then is the tear drawn, and only then can you put a crosshair on it
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_fissure.text_5: They are Create's goggles with a rift-ground lens, so they read every machine the engineer's pair does
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_fissure.text_6: Nothing breaks a fissure. The only way to be rid of one is to empty it
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_fissure_closing: The tear stands here, seen only through the goggles
Stand a Spatial Siphon within a few blocks of it. Nothing else is needed - no shaft, no redstone
The fissure hands its essence over steadily, and the tear shrinks as it empties
One holds several times what a single vessel does, so pipe it away or stand more than one nearby
A ring of siphons fills no faster. The tear is the limit, not the plumbing
Spent, it seals over for good. Nothing brings that one back
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_gate.text_1: Rift Gate Frame builds a ring standing upright, enclosing an empty opening
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_gate.text_2: The opening is the size limit. Whatever fits through it can travel - and nothing larger can
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_gate.text_3: Anything from four blocks of opening up to two hundred and twenty-five will form
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_gate.text_4: One block of the ring is a Rift Gate controller. It counts as frame, so it may sit anywhere in the circle
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_gate.text_5: A second gate has to be built somewhere else in the same world. A gate on its own goes nowhere
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_gate_dialling.t: Rotational force is what holds an aperture open. Let the speed drop and the gate hangs up
A wider opening is heavier to hold and dearer to dial, so a gate costs what it is worth
Rift Essence pays to dial, and keeps paying every second the doorway stands
Right-click the controller and choose which gate to reach for
Only the dialling gate pays. The far end needs no rotation and no essence of its own
Walk in, or drive in. A vehicle leaves the far gate the way that gate faces, carrying its speed with it
Both ends must lie in the same world. A gate cannot reach into another dimension
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_modulator.text_: A Rift Modulator bolted beside a Rift Drive lets its pilot choose the colour of the rift it tears, and even how it tears open
It reads whichever drive it happens to be touching, and takes its own facing from that drive the moment it is placed
It spends a trickle of Rift Essence, and only while the drive is actually running a warp - an idle drive costs it nothing
Right-click for a swatch of colours - left click sets the core, right click sets the rim - a theme to match, and how strongly it all reads
Run the tank dry, or take the module away, and the rift falls straight back to the drive's own tier colours
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_probe.text_1: Every other destination is somewhere a player carried an anchor to. A Rift Probe is how you reach ground nobody has stood on
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_probe.text_2: Right-click it, pick a direction on the dial and a distance on the slider, then scan ahead
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_probe.text_3: Rift Essence pays for each scan, and reaching further costs more. This is what a Spatial Siphon has been collecting for
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_probe.text_4: The wait is the world being made. A scan aimed at unexplored ground has to bring that ground into being before it can map it
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_probe.text_5: What comes back is the same chart the Astrolabe draws of an anchor - so a blind jump is judged on the same evidence as any other
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_probe.text_6: Send the ship there and the Rift Drive flies it. Bring an anchor: nothing marks the far end yet
aerowarptics.ponder.spatial_siphon.text_: A Spatial Siphon is built into an airship, not onto the ground
Passing a hull through folded space sheds something. Every siphon aboard catches a draught of it
Each one rolls separately, so a ship carrying several fills faster. Longer jumps are worth more
Four buckets fit inside. Pipes can draw the essence off into storage
Rift Essence is what dials a Rift Gate
aerowarptics.ponder.warp_anchor.text_1: A Warp Anchor is somewhere an airship can be sent
aerowarptics.ponder.warp_anchor.text_2: Right-click it to give it a name, and to say whether other players may travel to it
aerowarptics.ponder.warp_anchor.text_3: The world keeps the record, not the block. An anchor stays a valid destination while its chunks sleep
aerowarptics.ponder.warp_anchor.text_4: Leave room around it. An arriving hull has to fit, and the drive will refuse a berth that is blocked
